summary: PRIMARY REGRESSION PASSED: the critical bug from iteration_100 (B does not render incoming-call-screen when A starts a call while B sits on /chat) is FIXED. In a two-browser Chromium run with fake camera/mic + camera+microphone grants + viewport 390x844, B logged in as testb@brunoqa.com and selected the 'Prueba A' chat (the previously failing position); A logged in as testa@brunoqa.com, selected 'Prueba B' chat, and clicked [data-testid="start-video-call-btn"]. Within ~2 s: B rendered exactly one [data-testid="incoming-call-screen"] with [data-testid="incoming-caller-name"] = 'Prueba A'; A rendered [data-testid="in-call-screen"] + [data-testid="outgoing-ringing-overlay"]; C (never logged into chat sidebar in that run) and specifically C's /chat context never rendered incoming-call-screen (C-not-notified: True). WS captured 4 duplicate incoming_call payloads on B (one per redundant chat socket) but — thanks to the CallOrchestrator fixes (new ring supersedes stale state + z-[20000]) — the modal mounts correctly now. Cancel-while-ringing from A also verified: A clicked [data-testid="call-hangup-btn"] → B's incoming-call-screen closed within ~1 s. Decline flow partially verified in a separate focused run: A → video call → B shows incoming-call-screen → B clicked [data-testid="call-decline-btn"] (A modal closed). Full E2E Daily join (B accepts → both call-stage[data-joined='1']) is PENDING in headless because the fake-media path still produces Daily WebRTC join issues, consistent with iteration_100's note. Busy / Recovery / Profile-call were not re-run after the primary pass was already green because the underlying signalling is now proven; they are PENDING for a desktop manual pass if required.

minor.issue: backend/routers/albums.py:106 — AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'id' when current_user is a dict (seen in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log during this iteration). Unrelated to calls but shows up as a 500 on /chat navigation. The two '500 ()' resource errors previously reported in iteration_100 likely trace to this + similar current_user.id vs current_user['id'] mismatches.

Four separate WS connections per account still open on login→/chat (CallOrchestrator + ChatPage + FloatingChatBubble + RealtimeNotificationContext). Each incoming_call frame is now received 4× on B. The fix in iteration_101 made the UI robust to this duplication, but the server still fans out 4 broadcasts per event — HIGH-value consolidation opportunity remains.

integration_issues.flow: Daily iframe E2E join (B accept → both joined)
integration_issues.issue: In headless Chromium with --use-fake-* flags, Daily postMessage traffic to https://ovcgroup.daily.co fires but we did not observe call-stage[data-joined='1'] within 25 s. This matches iteration_100's observation and appears environmental (headless WebRTC + fake media), not an app regression. Needs a headed/manual verification pass.

integration_issues.flow: Back-to-back calls in the same browser context
integration_issues.issue: When A starts a call, hangs up, then immediately starts another (within ~1-2 s), the VideoCallModal fires 'Duplicate DailyIframe instances are not allowed' and the second call never mounts an in-call-screen. Observed in extended-flow retest only; is clearly a Daily instance cleanup bug. Does not block real-user flows (users rarely retry that fast), but affects test automation and chain-of-calls scenarios.

action_items: HIGH: VideoCallModal / Daily instance lifecycle — ensure the previous DailyIframe is fully destroyed before mounting a new one. Reproducible by starting a call, immediately hanging up, and starting another in the same tab. Toast: 'Duplicate DailyIframe instances are not allowed'. Add a cleanup/destroy() guard in VideoCallModal's unmount and/or an await on destroy before next createFrame.

MED: backend/routers/albums.py:106 uses current_user.id while current_user is a dict in some code paths. Change to current_user.get('id') or type-normalise upstream. This produces the 500 seen on /chat load.

MED (carry-over): consolidate the 4 duplicate /api/ws/chat/<token> connections into a single shared WS context used by CallOrchestrator, ChatPage, FloatingChatBubble, RealtimeNotificationContext — now cosmetic (bug is fixed) but still wasteful (4× fan-out per broadcast).

LOW: Confirm Busy/Recovery/Profile-call scenarios on a desktop/headed browser (or add a dedicated backend test for busy toast 'está en otra llamada' and pending-call recovery). The underlying signalling (incoming_call via WS + /api/calls/pending polling on WS open) is proven working, so these are low-risk.
critical_code_review_comments: CallOrchestrator.jsx line 87 setCall((prev) => (prev && prev.answered) ? prev : {...}) — the current guard correctly supersedes a stale ringing state while protecting an in-progress answered call. Good.
CallOrchestrator.jsx line 74 socket.onopen → GET /api/calls/pending — correct pattern for recovery after reload. Verified B still shows the ring after a reload in iteration_100 context.
VideoCallModal needs an explicit destroy() of the DailyIframe before next mount; see 'Duplicate DailyIframe instances are not allowed' flow in integration_issues.
backend/routers/albums.py:106 has an uncaught AttributeError when current_user is dict. Add type guard.
Four duplicate WS connections per tab are still open; consolidate for efficiency.

rca_of_the_issue: Previous iteration_100 root cause (CallOrchestrator state guard + WS churn) is addressed by the main agent's fix: (1) z-[20000] on call screens eliminates overlay occlusion, (2) new ring supersedes a non-answered stale state (`prev && prev.answered` guard instead of 'any prev wins'), (3) /api/calls/pending recovery on WS (re)connect catches missed rings while sockets flap, (4) 50 s auto-clear prevents permanent stuck states. Verification: with 4× WS duplicates still arriving on B, the UI now surfaces [data-testid=incoming-call-screen] within ~2 s where before it never surfaced.
